svg.text: WHAT THE MODEL SAYS
WHAT IT DRAWS
Both symptoms come from the same shape: this path writes to two stores that cannot
commit together, and it acknowledges work before the work is durable.
The loss is between the claim and the enqueue. SETNX event_id in Redis and XADD to
webhook-events are two independent writes. If the process dies, the pod is evicted, or
the produce times out after Redis has said "new", the event is marked seen and no
message exists. Stripe sees the failure and retries — and the retry makes it worse:
SETNX returns 0, the endpoint returns 202, and the second attempt is discarded because
the first one failed. No error, no DLQ row, and Stripe correctly reports delivery.
Make the claim and the message durable together. The cheap fix: do not return 202 until
the produce has succeeded, and make the claim two-phase — pending before the produce,
done after — so a retry that finds pending republishes instead of deduping. The thorough
fix removes Redis from the ack path: insert the raw event into an inbox table and
publish from a poller, so the claim and the intent to publish are one commit. An outbox
written by the transaction that changes the order is the same idea with the order as the
source of truth.
The duplicates are the same problem one hop later. If the consumer commits its Kafka
offset before the Postgres commit lands — or auto-commits on a timer — a crash in
between redelivers the message. That is harmless only if the handler is idempotent:
UPDATE orders SET status = 'paid' WHERE id = $2 AND status <> 'paid' is; balance =
balance + amount, or a capture call to Stripe, is not. Key the effect on event_id, not
on delivery count, and ack after COMMIT with manual commit.
The third window is the DLQ. An event that fails three times is parked, but the endpoint
already returned 202 and the event_id is seen, so no retry brings it back. The DLQ needs
an alarm and a replay command, or it is where events go to be forgotten.
The rule that ties it together: the dedupe record must live in the same durability
domain as the effect it guards, and the ack must come after the durable effect, not
after the attempt.
384 WORDS, READ IN ORDER
23 OPS, DRAWN AS IT TALKS
